news.headline: US-Iran Military Conflict Drives Crude Oil Up ~9% Last Week
news.what_happened: The US struck three Iranian oil tankers over the weekend following Iranian ballistic missile attacks on US warships. This triggered the strongest weekly crude gain since mid-July, with WTI trading in the $82.67-$94.91 range.
news.why_it_matters: India imports ~85% of its crude. This oil spike hits India's current account deficit, weakens the INR (now at 94.45), raises input costs for airlines, paints, tyres, logistics and FMCG, while directly boosting ONGC/OIL realizations and giving OMCs short-term inventory gains.

news.headline: USD/INR at 94.45 — Rupee at Multi-Year Lows
news.what_happened: The Indian Rupee has weakened to ~94.42-94.50 per USD, driven by the crude oil surge increasing import costs and FII outflows.
news.why_it_matters: A weaker rupee dramatically boosts INR earnings for export-oriented companies. IT firms (TCS, INFY, WIPRO, HCLTECH) and pharma exporters (SUNPHARMA, DRREDDY, CIPLA) report in INR but earn primarily in USD — every rupee of depreciation directly expands margins.

news.headline: US Markets Closed Today (Labor Day); Last Close S&P -0.38%
news.what_happened: US markets are closed Monday Sept 7 for Labor Day. Last session (Sept 5): S&P 500 -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.29%, Dow -0.51%. Asian markets are positive: Nikkei +1%, Kospi +3.09%.
news.why_it_matters: Absence of US direction reduces FII activity today. Indian markets driven by domestic flows and energy sector developments. Asian positivity provides partial support.

news.headline: FII Net Sellers Rs 3,112 Cr; DII Bought Rs 8,930 Cr (Sept 4 data)
news.what_happened: Foreign institutions sold Rs 3,111.90 Cr while domestic institutions (LIC, MFs) bought Rs 8,930.10 Cr in the last session — providing strong domestic support against FII outflows.
news.why_it_matters: With US markets closed today limiting FII participation, domestic flows will be the dominant market driver. Strong DII buying cushion supports midcaps and PSUs.

news.headline: China Manufacturing PMI Contracts for Second Consecutive Month
news.what_happened: China's factory activity shrank for the second straight month through late August 2026, signaling weakening industrial demand from the world's largest commodity consumer.
news.why_it_matters: China is the largest buyer of steel, aluminum and copper. Contracting PMI signals weaker demand and pressures global metal prices. Indian metal producers face earnings headwinds.

news.headline: India GDP Q1 FY27 at 7.8%; Sovereign Rating Upgraded to A-
news.what_happened: India recorded 7.8% GDP growth in Q1 FY2026-27 with manufacturing GVA up 9.2%. Sovereign rating lifted to 'A-'. Exports rose 13% to $316 billion in April-July FY27.
news.why_it_matters: Strong macro fundamentals support domestic-oriented and capital goods sectors. Rating upgrade could attract long-term FII inflows. Infrastructure and capex-linked names remain structural buys.

picks.catalyst: WTI Crude up ~9% last week due to US-Iran military conflict; geopolitical premium likely to persist
picks.logic: ONGC is India's largest upstream oil producer. Every $1 rise in crude oil price improves ONGC's annual realization by ~Rs 2,000 Cr+. With WTI in $82-95 range vs prior baseline, realization is materially higher. US-Iran tensions show no sign of quick resolution, sustaining the geopolitical crude premium. Direct, quantifiable P&L impact.

picks.catalyst: USD/INR at 94.45 — rupee at multi-year lows; direct margin expansion for USD revenue earner
picks.logic: TCS earns ~70% of revenues in USD/foreign currency and reports in INR. At 94.45 vs prior 83-84 baseline, INR earnings are structurally 11-12% higher. With US markets closed today (no FII selling pressure), IT stocks may see domestic-driven accumulation. No negative US tech catalyst to counter the currency tailwind.

picks.catalyst: Crude surge creates short-term inventory gains for downstream OMC; also has upstream exposure
picks.logic: HPCL holds significant crude oil and product inventory. A sharp weekly crude surge means inventory on its books is worth more — creating accounting gains in the near term. HPCL also has upstream equity participation in oil blocks. While medium-term margins face pressure if retail prices aren't adjusted, the immediate inventory gain is a real near-term P&L tailwind. Risk: government may cap fuel price hikes.
